purpose: Frozen question/answer pairs for the M5 Phase 2 agent comparison between the real DSH default retrieval tools and the code-intelligence context_* tools. Deterministically derived from the frozen gold; contains no tool-specific tuning. Tasks are partitioned into natural, conformance, and tool-shaped layers.

sources.v1WordingChange: question text only; answerSpec values are byte-identical to v1

rules.questions: Every arm receives the byte-identical question text; the task set is frozen before any arm runs.
rules.answers: Grading is programmatic against answerSpec: exact string equality for text and path, exact integer equality for lines, and set answers require unique elements plus exact normalized equality (duplicates are incorrect).
rules.leakage: No question names a tool or a tool argument. The gold request fields (name/kind/pathPrefix/offsets/lineRange/types) are restated in plain language because they define the task, not the method. Seven v1 questions restated them in the tested tool's own vocabulary (UTF-16 code-unit offsets, padding/clamping, named relation types); v2 removes that vocabulary without changing any expected answer.
rules.vocabulary: Each task carries a `vocabulary` field: natural semantic retrieval, conformance/coordinate contract, or tool-shaped diagnostic. Layers are reported separately and never pooled.
rules.independence: This file and its generator never call the tested extractor or any tool; they only project eval/m5/gold.json.
rules.scope: This is a retrieval QA benchmark over a frozen corpus, not a SWE task benchmark. It measures whether an agent can obtain and report repository facts, not whether it can change code.

vocabularyPolicy.natural: Declaration and relation questions expressed without tool-specific request vocabulary.
vocabularyPolicy.conformance: Source-coordinate and exact-byte questions that test a frozen API contract.
vocabularyPolicy.rule: Natural, conformance, and tool-shaped layers are reported separately and never pooled.

budget.note: Identical caps for every arm. An arm that exceeds a cap fails that task.
